scope: Approved phases 0–2: workflow cohesion, editable annotations, watermark designer

phases.name: Workflow cohesion
implemented: Validate and deduplicate explicit workspace action IDs; exclude retained hidden sources without excluding filtered selections.
Prevent blocked conversion entry from clearing profiles or conversion state.
Expose Annotate Photo and Open Photos as Layers in workspace actions.
Preserve independent workspace selection, batch inputs and document state.
verification: 12 native Mac output/scope regression tests passed at phase checkpoint.
remaining: Further recipe, command palette and creation/export bridges follow these phases.

phases.name: Editable annotation
implemented: Translucent editable highlights and semantic numbered callouts in existing annotation pipeline.
Automatic callout renumbering after order changes or deletion, persisted identities, Undo/Redo.
Editable speech-bubble text controls; annotation order controls and consistent labels.
Preview/export parity tests and source-byte preservation.
verification: Phase checkpoint: 163 Core tests, 3 opt-in skips, 0 failures.
Phase checkpoint: 29 native Mac tests, 0 failures; iOS build succeeded.
Final Core and mobile suites include annotation export, blending, round-trip and undo tests.
remaining: Live mouse/touch/Pencil, VoiceOver and dense overlapping-object interaction checks remain manual.

phases.name: Watermark designer
implemented: 12 original editable templates using existing EditorDocument text, shape and image layers.
Installed-font editing, transforms, opacity, ordering, visibility, locking, duplication and editable text outlines/shadows.
Local named version-2 design packages with embedded resources, import, edit and deletion.
Dark/light/checkerboard authoring previews; backgrounds excluded from design output.
Explicit captured photo targets; one grouped undoable application preserving placement and unrelated edits.
Immutable applied image snapshots rendered through the existing layer and watermark engines.
High-resolution vector stamp rendering, bounded to 16 MP per application; no competing composition renderer.
Import/application on iPhone and iPad, compact and accessibility layouts.
verification: Final Core: 167 tests, 3 opt-in skips, 0 failures.
Final iPhone: 57 tests, 0 failures; successful complete Xcode result.
Final iPad: 57 tests, 0 failures; successful complete Xcode result.
Release-tool tests: 2 passed. Static preflight: 0 failures, existing submission blockers.
Native hosted Mac designer/template and mobile library normal/large-text captures inspected.
remaining: Full multi-element authoring currently requires Mac.
No real-device or VoiceOver/Pencil validation; native UI automation pipe cannot start.
Photograph background preview currently uses reversible application in the photo editor; designer offers solid/checkerboard backgrounds.
Template art direction is an original first collection and still needs broader photographic/print review.
No M1/8 GB performance target or hundreds-of-images physical-device acceptance claim.

compatibility: Legacy text/image watermarks and document version 1 remain supported. New designer metadata and text treatments require version 2 to prevent older editors silently dropping them. Internal Framepebble modules/storage/bundle identities are retained.
known_environment_issues: Native computer control fails with Sky Computer Use native pipe startup failed. Captures populate hosted native views programmatically, not by simulated user input.
Mac test host continues logging MDB_MAP_FULL; origin is unresolved.
An initial iPhone run completed all assertions but stalled finalizing its result bundle. Complete iPhone and iPad retries succeeded with automatic diagnostic collection disabled.
Existing public privacy/support URLs and signed distribution artifacts remain submission blockers.
follow_on: Reusable recipes with source-specific geometry/Auto Enhance handling.
Command-K routing to existing explicitly scoped actions.
Creation/export integration and further watermark preview/application refinements.
